# Provider test fixtures

Every fixture is hand-modeled from the parsing logic of the frozen Python
original (`/home/whoami/projects/anicli-py`, branch `snapshot/broken-2026-09-12`):
each file reproduces the minimal real-world response shape the referenced
Python code consumes. No fixture is a byte-for-byte network capture; fields
irrelevant to the parsing logic are trimmed. If the live API drifts, the
provenance reference below points at the Python parsing code that defines
the expected input.

Fixtures marked **[LIVE-VERIFIED …]** diverge from that rule on
purpose: they are derived from real network captures of the marked day
(2026-09-13 for the matcher-oracle wave, 2026-09-17 for the torrent
providers, 2026-09-18 for the third revival wave — animevost,
sameband, animego.me, gogoanime → Anitaku —
and the anizone wave, PR59, which has no Python original at all and is
pinned against the Anivexa-API recipe instead;
page chrome trimmed, values verbatim) because the live site drifted
away from the frozen Python shapes — see the per-fixture notes.

Rows follow the factory registration order
(`internal/providers/factory.go`). Every file under this directory has
exactly one row; deleting or renaming a fixture must update its row in
the same change.
